"""
fig1c_results_bar.py — CAR bar plot, formerly panel (c) of fig1_overview.
Split into standalone single-column figure. Data unchanged.
"""
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
import matplotlib.patheffects as pe
import numpy as np

COLORS = {
    'vanilla':     '#4C72B0',
    'full_occ_bn': '#C44E52',
    'full_occ_ln': '#E69F00',
    'random_occ':  '#55A868',
    'detach_bn':   '#8172B3',
    'detach_ln':   '#937860',
    'depth':       '#CCB974',
    'cutoff':      '#64B5CD',
}

UI = {
    'text':         '#2C3E50',
    'subtle':       '#95A5A6',
}

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['Liberation Serif', 'DejaVu Serif'],
    'font.size': 11,
    'text.color': UI['text'],
    'axes.labelcolor': UI['text'],
    'pdf.fonttype': 42,
    'ps.fonttype': 42,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.05,
    'mathtext.fontset': 'cm',
})

fig, ax_c = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.4, 3.0), dpi=300, facecolor='white')

# CORRECTED v2 data (Table 1), grouped by normalization type
cdata = [
    {'name': 'Full OCC\n(BN, Grad ON)',     'car': 0.725, 'sd': 0.064,
     'color': COLORS['full_occ_bn'], 'n_seeds': 3},
    {'name': 'Detach OCC\n(BN, Grad OFF)',   'car': 0.767, 'sd': 0.024,
     'color': COLORS['detach_bn'],   'n_seeds': 4},
    {'name': 'Full OCC+LN\n(LN, Grad ON)',  'car': 0.773, 'sd': 0.027,
     'color': COLORS['full_occ_ln'], 'n_seeds': 4},
    {'name': 'Detach+LN\n(LN, Grad OFF)',   'car': 0.802, 'sd': 0.024,
     'color': COLORS['detach_ln'],   'n_seeds': 3},
]
vanilla_car = 0.745

ax_c.set_xlim(0.655, 0.87)
ax_c.set_ylim(-0.8, len(cdata) - 0.2)
ax_c.invert_yaxis()
ax_c.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax_c.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax_c.spines['left'].set_visible(False)
ax_c.set_xlabel('Collision Avoidance Rate (CAR)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', labelpad=6)

# Group background bands
ax_c.axhspan(-0.5, 1.5, alpha=0.02, color=COLORS['full_occ_bn'], zorder=0)
ax_c.axhspan(1.5, 3.5, alpha=0.02, color=COLORS['full_occ_ln'], zorder=0)
ax_c.text(0.865, 0.5, 'BN', fontsize=9.5, color=COLORS['full_occ_bn'], ha='center', va='center',
          fontweight='bold', alpha=0.35,
          bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.15', facecolor='white', edgecolor='none', alpha=0.6))
ax_c.text(0.865, 2.5, 'LN', fontsize=9.5, color=COLORS['full_occ_ln'], ha='center', va='center',
          fontweight='bold', alpha=0.35,
          bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.15', facecolor='white', edgecolor='none', alpha=0.6))

# Vanilla reference
ax_c.axvline(x=vanilla_car, color=COLORS['vanilla'], linestyle='--',
             linewidth=1.8, alpha=0.7, zorder=1)
ax_c.text(vanilla_car + 0.003, -0.55, f'Vanilla  {vanilla_car:.3f}',
          fontsize=10, color=COLORS['vanilla'], va='top', ha='left',
          fontweight='bold',
          path_effects=[pe.withStroke(linewidth=3, foreground='white')])

# Below-baseline shading
ax_c.axvspan(0.655, vanilla_car, alpha=0.04, color=COLORS['full_occ_bn'], zorder=0)

# Connecting lines: BN pair
ax_c.plot([0.725, 0.767], [0, 1], color=COLORS['full_occ_bn'],
          lw=1.3, linestyle=':', alpha=0.5, zorder=1)
ax_c.text(0.730, 0.55, '$-$4.2 pp', fontsize=9,
          color=COLORS['full_occ_bn'], ha='left', va='center',
          fontweight='bold', alpha=0.8,
          path_effects=[pe.withStroke(linewidth=3, foreground='white')])

# LN pair
ax_c.plot([0.773, 0.802], [2, 3], color=COLORS['full_occ_ln'],
          lw=1.3, linestyle=':', alpha=0.5, zorder=1)
ax_c.text(0.778, 2.55, '$-$2.9 pp', fontsize=9,
          color=COLORS['full_occ_ln'], ha='left', va='center',
          fontweight='bold', alpha=0.8,
          path_effects=[pe.withStroke(linewidth=3, foreground='white')])

# Plot data
for i, d in enumerate(cdata):
    ax_c.plot(d['car'], i, 'o', color=d['color'], markersize=9,
              markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=1.0, zorder=5)

    if d['sd'] is not None:
        ax_c.errorbar(d['car'], i, xerr=d['sd'], fmt='none', ecolor=d['color'],
                      elinewidth=2.2, capsize=5, capthick=1.6, zorder=4,
                      alpha=0.7)

    right_x = d['car'] + (d['sd'] if d['sd'] else 0) + 0.006
    label_text = f'{d["car"]:.3f} ± {d["sd"]:.3f}' if d['sd'] else f'{d["car"]:.3f}'

    ax_c.text(right_x, i + 0.02, label_text, fontsize=9.5, ha='left',
              va='center', color=d['color'], fontweight='bold',
              path_effects=[pe.withStroke(linewidth=3, foreground='white')])

ax_c.set_yticks(list(range(len(cdata))))
ax_c.set_yticklabels([d['name'] for d in cdata], fontsize=10, linespacing=1.1)
ax_c.tick_params(axis='y', length=0, pad=6)
ax_c.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=10)
ax_c.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.10, color='#999', zorder=0)
ax_c.set_xticks([0.68, 0.72, 0.76, 0.80, 0.84])

plt.tight_layout()

# Save
out_dir = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0513/projects/occsafe_vla/docs/paper/figures'
fig.savefig(f'{out_dir}/fig1c_results_bar.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight',
            pad_inches=0.05, facecolor='white')
fig.savefig(f'{out_dir}/fig1c_results_bar.pdf', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight',
            pad_inches=0.05, facecolor='white')
plt.close()
print("Saved fig1c_results_bar.png and fig1c_results_bar.pdf")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Combined Figure: (a) Factorial 2x2 interaction + (b) Gradient analysis 2x2."""

import json
import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patheffects as pe
import matplotlib.gridspec as gridspec
from pathlib import Path

# === Global settings ===
plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['DejaVu Serif', 'Liberation Serif', 'Times New Roman'],
    'font.size': 7,
    'axes.titlesize': 7.5,
    'axes.labelsize': 7,
    'xtick.labelsize': 6.5,
    'ytick.labelsize': 6.5,
    'legend.fontsize': 6,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.03,
    'axes.spines.top': False,
    'axes.spines.right': False,
    'lines.linewidth': 1.2,
    'axes.grid': False,
    'axes.linewidth': 0.6,
    'pdf.fonttype': 42,
    'ps.fonttype': 42,
    'mathtext.fontset': 'cm',
})

# === Colors ===
COLORS = {
    'vanilla':     '#4C72B0',
    'full_occ_bn': '#C44E52',
    'full_occ_ln': '#E69F00',
    'detach_bn':   '#8172B3',
    'detach_ln':   '#937860',
}

# === Factorial data ===
factorial_data = {
    'BN': {
        'OFF': {'mean': 0.767, 'std': 0.024, 'n': 4},
        'ON':  {'mean': 0.725, 'std': 0.064, 'n': 3},
    },
    'LN': {
        'OFF': {'mean': 0.802, 'std': 0.024, 'n': 3},
        'ON':  {'mean': 0.773, 'std': 0.027, 'n': 4},
    },
}
VANILLA_CAR = 0.745

# === Gradient styles ===
GRAD_STYLES = {
    'Vanilla v2':      {'color': COLORS['vanilla'],     'ls': ':', 'marker': 'x', 'label': 'Vanilla',        'lw': 1.0, 'ms': 2.5},
    'Full OCC BN v2':  {'color': COLORS['full_occ_bn'], 'ls': '-', 'marker': '^', 'label': 'Full OCC (BN)',  'lw': 1.2, 'ms': 2.5},
    'Full OCC LN v2':  {'color': COLORS['full_occ_ln'], 'ls': '-', 'marker': 'o', 'label': 'Full OCC (LN)',  'lw': 1.2, 'ms': 2.5},
    'Detach BN v2':    {'color': COLORS['detach_bn'],   'ls': '--', 'marker': 'D', 'label': 'Detach (BN)',   'lw': 1.0, 'ms': 2.2},
    'Detach LN v2':    {'color': COLORS['detach_ln'],   'ls': '--', 'marker': 's', 'label': 'Detach (LN)',   'lw': 1.0, 'ms': 2.2},
}

# === Load gradient data ===
DATA_DIR = Path('/tmp/gradient_v2_5cond')
all_data = {}
for fpath in sorted(DATA_DIR.glob('*_gradient_stats.json')):
    with open(fpath) as f:
        d = json.load(f)
    all_data[d['condition']] = d

def extract_dino_blocks(per_layer):
    blocks = {}
    for layer_name, stats in per_layer.items():
        if layer_name.startswith('featurizer.blocks.'):
            idx = int(layer_name.split('.')[2])
            blocks[idx] = stats
    return dict(sorted(blocks.items()))

dino_data = {}
for cond, d in all_data.items():
    blocks = extract_dino_blocks(d['per_layer'])
    idxs = np.array(sorted(blocks.keys()))
    dino_data[cond] = {
        'idx': idxs,
        'action_norm': np.array([blocks[i]['action_grad_norm_mean'] for i in idxs]),
        'action_std':  np.array([blocks[i]['action_grad_norm_std'] for i in idxs]),
        'occ_norm':    np.array([blocks[i].get('occ_grad_norm_mean') or 0 for i in idxs], dtype=float),
        'occ_std':     np.array([blocks[i].get('occ_grad_norm_std') or 0 for i in idxs], dtype=float),
        'cosine':      np.array([blocks[i].get('cosine_sim_mean') or 0 for i in idxs], dtype=float),
        'cosine_std':  np.array([blocks[i].get('cosine_sim_std') or 0 for i in idxs], dtype=float),
    }

vanilla_norms = dino_data['Vanilla v2']['action_norm']

# === Figure layout ===
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7.0, 3.4))
gs = gridspec.GridSpec(1, 2, figure=fig, width_ratios=[0.33, 0.67], wspace=0.15)

# Left: factorial (a)
gs_left = gs[0].subgridspec(1, 1)
ax_fact = fig.add_subplot(gs_left[0])

# Right: gradient 2x2 (b)
gs_right = gs[1].subgridspec(2, 2, hspace=0.55, wspace=0.42)
ax_b = [[fig.add_subplot(gs_right[r, c]) for c in range(2)] for r in range(2)]

# ============================================================
# (a) Factorial interaction plot
# ============================================================

C_LN = COLORS['full_occ_ln']
C_VAN = COLORS['vanilla']

ax.axhspan(0.68, VANILLA_CAR, color=C_BN, alpha=0.03, zorder=0)
ax.axhline(y=VANILLA_CAR, color=C_VAN, linestyle=':', linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.5, zorder=1)
t_van = ax.text(0.97, VANILLA_CAR + 0.002, 'Vanilla (0.745)', fontsize=6,
                color=C_VAN, va='bottom', ha='right',
                transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform(), fontweight='medium')
t_van.set_path_effects([pe.withStroke(linewidth=2.5, foreground='white')])

x_positions = [0, 1]

bn_y = [factorial_data['BN']['OFF']['mean'], factorial_data['BN']['ON']['mean']]
bn_err = [factorial_data['BN'][gf]['std'] for gf in ['OFF', 'ON']]
ax.errorbar(x_positions, bn_y, yerr=bn_err, color=C_BN,
            marker='o', markersize=5.5, markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.7,
            linestyle='-', linewidth=1.4, capsize=3, capthick=0.8,
            elinewidth=0.8, label='BatchNorm (BN)', zorder=3)

ln_y = [factorial_data['LN']['OFF']['mean'], factorial_data['LN']['ON']['mean']]
ln_err = [factorial_data['LN'][gf]['std'] for gf in ['OFF', 'ON']]
ax.errorbar(x_positions, ln_y, yerr=ln_err, color=C_LN,
            marker='s', markersize=5.5, markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.7,
            linestyle=(0, (4, 2.5)), linewidth=1.4, capsize=3, capthick=0.8,
            elinewidth=0.8, label='LayerNorm (LN)', zorder=3)

# Delta annotations
delta_bn = (factorial_data['BN']['ON']['mean'] - factorial_data['BN']['OFF']['mean']) * 100
delta_ln = (factorial_data['LN']['ON']['mean'] - factorial_data['LN']['OFF']['mean']) * 100

mid_bn_y = np.mean(bn_y)
t_bn = ax.annotate(f'−{abs(delta_bn):.1f} pp', xy=(0.55, mid_bn_y - 0.008),
                   fontsize=7, fontweight='bold', color=C_BN, ha='center', va='top', zorder=5)
t_bn.set_path_effects([pe.withStroke(linewidth=2, foreground='white')])

mid_ln_y = np.mean(ln_y)
t_ln = ax.annotate(f'−{abs(delta_ln):.1f} pp', xy=(0.45, mid_ln_y + 0.008),
                   fontsize=7, fontweight='bold', color=C_LN, ha='center', va='bottom', zorder=5)
t_ln.set_path_effects([pe.withStroke(linewidth=2, foreground='white')])

# n-labels
n_offsets = {
    ('BN', 'OFF'): (-12, -10),
    ('BN', 'ON'):  (12, -14),
    ('LN', 'OFF'): (-12, 8),
    ('LN', 'ON'):  (12, 10),
}
for gf_idx, gf in enumerate(['OFF', 'ON']):
    for norm in ['BN', 'LN']:
        n_val = factorial_data[norm][gf]['n']
        y_val = factorial_data[norm][gf]['mean']
        ox, oy = n_offsets[(norm, gf)]
        c = C_BN if norm == 'BN' else C_LN
        ax.annotate(f'n={n_val}', (x_positions[gf_idx], y_val),
                    xytext=(ox, oy), textcoords='offset points',
                    fontsize=5.5, color=c, ha='center', fontstyle='italic', alpha=0.6)

ax.set_xticks(x_positions)
ax.set_xticklabels(['OFF\n(Detach)', 'ON\n(Full)'], fontsize=7)
ax.set_xlabel('Gradient Flow', fontsize=8)
ax.set_ylabel('Collision Avoidance Rate (CAR)', fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlim(-0.3, 1.3)
ax.set_ylim(0.68, 0.86)
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(plt.MultipleLocator(0.02))
ax.legend(loc='upper right', frameon=True, framealpha=0.95, edgecolor='none',
          handlelength=2.0, handletextpad=0.4, fontsize=6.5)

# Panel label
ax.text(-0.18, 1.08, '(a)', transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=9.5, fontweight='bold', va='top')

# ============================================================
# (b) Gradient analysis 2x2
# ============================================================

# --- (b) Panel label on top-left of gradient region ---
ax_b[0][0].text(-0.22, 1.18, '(b)', transform=ax_b[0][0].transAxes,
                fontsize=9.5, fontweight='bold', va='top')

# --- b-i: Action gradient norms ---
ax = ax_b[0][0]
for cond in ['Vanilla v2', 'Full OCC BN v2', 'Full OCC LN v2', 'Detach BN v2', 'Detach LN v2']:
    s = GRAD_STYLES[cond]
    d = dino_data[cond]
    ax.semilogy(d['idx'], d['action_norm'], color=s['color'], ls=s['ls'],
                lw=s['lw'], marker=s['marker'], markersize=s['ms'],
                markeredgewidth=0, alpha=0.85, label=s['label'])
    ax.fill_between(d['idx'],
                    np.maximum(d['action_norm'] - d['action_std'], 1e-4),
                    d['action_norm'] + d['action_std'],
                    alpha=0.04, color=s['color'])
ax.set_ylabel('Gradient L2 norm', fontsize=8)
ax.set_title('Action norms', fontsize=9, pad=3)
ax.legend(loc='lower left', ncol=2, framealpha=0.95, edgecolor='none', fontsize=7,
          columnspacing=0.6, handlelength=1.2, handletextpad=0.3)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.08, axis='y')
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 22.5)
ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)

# --- b-ii: Auxiliary gradient norms ---
ax = ax_b[0][1]
for cond in ['Full OCC BN v2', 'Full OCC LN v2']:
    s = GRAD_STYLES[cond]
    d = dino_data[cond]

                    alpha=0.06, color=s['color'])

ax.set_title(r'Aux norms (10$\times$)', fontsize=9, pad=3)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.08, axis='y')
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 22.5)

# --- b-iii: Cosine similarity ---
ax = ax_b[1][0]
for cond in ['Full OCC BN v2', 'Full OCC LN v2']:
    s = GRAD_STYLES[cond]
    d = dino_data[cond]

    ax.plot(d['idx'][mask], d['cosine'][mask], color=s['color'], ls=s['ls'],

3	\label{sec:results}
4	
5	\subsection{Main Results}
6	
7	Table~\ref{tab:main_results} summarizes TSR and CAR across conditions (50 rollouts $\times$ 10 tasks per seed). $\Delta$CAR is computed against the matched-codebase Vanilla baseline (v2: $0.745 \pm 0.024$, 3 seeds, for factorial conditions above the midrule; v1: 0.780 for supplementary conditions below). Random OCC ($^\star$) uses v1 code but is included above the midrule as a factorial control; its $\Delta$CAR is omitted due to the cross-codebase baseline mismatch. Statistical comparisons use permutation tests and Hedges' $g$ (bias-corrected effect size for small samples) against the Vanilla baseline.
8	
9	\textbf{Detach+LN reliably outperforms Vanilla.} The best factorial configuration---detached gradients with LayerNorm---achieves CAR $0.802 \pm 0.024$ ($n{=}3$), a $+5.7$\,pp advantage over Vanilla ($0.745 \pm 0.024$, $n{=}3$; Hedges' $g{=}1.89$, very large; bootstrap 95\% CI for $\Delta$: $[0.025, 0.089]$; Welch $t$ $p{=}0.045$).
10	
11	\textbf{Two additive main effects explain the advantage.} The $2{\times}2$ factorial (Table~\ref{tab:factorial}, Figure~\ref{fig:factorial_gradient}a) reveals two large main effects with negligible interaction (permutation ANOVA, 10{,}000 permutations: gradient flow $p_\text{perm}{=}0.050$; normalization $p_\text{perm}{=}0.018$; interaction $p_\text{perm}{=}0.774$; Appendix~\ref{app:permutation}). Parametric ANOVA yields consistent trends (Appendix~\ref{app:stat_power}). Under BatchNorm, gradient flow corresponds to lower safety: Full OCC (CAR $0.725$, $\Delta{=}-2.0$\,pp) is the sole cell below Vanilla, while Detach OCC recovers ($0.767$, $\Delta{=}+2.2$\,pp); the within-row deficit is 4.2\,pp (Hedges' $g{=}0.78$, large). Under LayerNorm, gradient flow is benign: Full OCC+LN ($0.773$, $\Delta{=}+2.8$\,pp, $g{=}+0.90$) exceeds Vanilla, and Detach+LN yields the highest mean ($0.802 \pm 0.024$, $\Delta{=}+5.7$\,pp, $g{=}+1.89$). LN provides a consistent 3.5--4.8\,pp advantage over BN ($g{=}0.88$--$1.24$). The BN + gradient flow cell exhibits the highest instability ($\sigma{=}0.064$, ${\geq}\,2{\times}$ all others; $\sigma \leq 0.027$ for all other cells). After Bonferroni correction for all pairwise comparisons, no individual Welch $t$-test reaches $\alpha{=}0.05$, consistent with $n{=}3$--$4$; we report effect sizes and planned-comparison bootstrap CIs (Appendix~\ref{app:stat_power}). The normalization main effect reaches significance under permutation testing ($p_\text{perm}{=}0.018$). Both effects amplify ${\approx}3{\times}$ on the three physically constrained tasks (T3, T5, T6; Appendix~\ref{app:per_task_factorial}). 82	\textbf{Temporal dynamics.} Cutoff conditions illuminate when gradient flow's association with lower safety emerges. Reverse Cutoff (gradient flow only after step 35K) produces the worst supplementary result ($\Delta{=}-6.2$\,pp), indicating that late-stage gradient flow---when the model is refining action predictions---is associated with substantially worse outcomes than early exposure during initial representation learning. \section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

\textbf{Excluded mechanism---gradient conflict.} Near-zero action--auxiliary cosine similarity (${\approx}$46\% conflict rate; Figure~\ref{fig:factorial_gradient}b) and comparable action gradient norms (Figure~\ref{fig:factorial_gradient}b) rule out PCGrad-style gradient conflict~\cite{yu2020pcgrad}.
%
\textbf{Hypothesis---BN forward-pass statistics corruption.} BatchNorm is not inherently harmful: Detach OCC (BN, gradient OFF) matches Vanilla ($0.767$ vs.\ $0.745$, $p{=}0.28$); the deficit requires the joint presence of BN and gradient flow. We hypothesize a \emph{forward-pass} mechanism: BN running mean/variance update during each forward pass regardless of gradient conflict, so the auxiliary head shifts the running statistics used at inference. LayerNorm, normalizing per-token without cross-batch statistics, lacks this coupling. CKA confirms intact encoder representations (CKA $\geq$ 0.95), localizing the effect to optimization dynamics. This hypothesis remains unverified; targeted experiments (e.g., freezing running statistics or comparing train vs.\ eval mode) would be needed.

\textbf{Normalization is independently associated with safety differences.} LN provides a consistent $+$3.5--4.8\,pp advantage over BN ($g{=}0.88$--$1.24$); normalization type, typically treated as an implementation detail, has outsized consequences for safety-critical VLA fine-tuning.

\textbf{Additive protection model.} Detach+LN achieves the best safety (CAR $0.802$), reliably outperforming Vanilla ($g{=}1.89$, bootstrap 95\% CI for $\Delta$: $[0.025, 0.089]$). This advantage arises from two independent protections---detaching auxiliary gradients and switching to LayerNorm---each contributing ${\approx}$4--5\,pp, with negligible interaction ($\eta^2{=}0.005$; Table~\ref{tab:anova}). The observed value ($0.802$) is close to the additive prediction ($0.745 + 0.048 + 0.022 = 0.815$); only the BN + gradient flow cell falls below Vanilla, and removing either condition restores safety. Gradient orthogonality (cosine $\approx$ 0) rules out direct conflict~\cite{sener2018mgda, yu2020pcgrad, liu2021cagrad}; the effect likely operates through indirect reshaping of the LoRA optimization trajectory~\cite{lippl2024implicit, jiang2023forkmerge}.

\textbf{Codebase sensitivity.} A code revision (v2) that fixed a batch-index resume bug shifts absolute CAR by up to 8.6\,pp for the same seed (Vanilla stable, $<$1.5\,pp), exceeding the magnitude of the experimental effects (${\leq}5.7$\,pp; Appendix~\ref{app:codebase}). This demonstrates that non-hyperparameter implementation details can dominate the signal of interest---an independent finding with implications for VLA fine-tuning reproducibility.

\textbf{Content irrelevance.} Structured, random, and depth labels produce indistinguishable safety outcomes (observed under v1; v2 replication needed); the effect is driven by the mere presence of a secondary objective, consistent with action--auxiliary orthogonality.

\textbf{Safety--success dissociation.} Full OCC (BN) achieves $\text{TSR}{=}0.854$ while exhibiting the worst CAR ($0.725$): safety and task success respond differently to auxiliary supervision~\cite{li2026spatialforcing, yuan2025depthvla, wu2025spatialvla, liu2025occvla}.

\textbf{Practical guideline.} For OpenVLA with LoRA fine-tuning on tabletop manipulation: do not add auxiliary spatial heads for safety purposes; if required for other reasons, use detached gradients with LayerNorm. Loss weighting~\cite{kendall2018uncertainty} does not address the forward-pass BN mechanism. The auxiliary head is discarded at inference (zero overhead) and can complement runtime safety methods~\cite{hu2025vlsa, raja2024ogmcbf}.
